1.explanation:
The root of the problem lives in the Storybook setup inside UIShell.stories.js. The default export for the CSF file does not declare a `component` nor list its `subcomponents`, so the Docs addon can’t infer which component the `<Props />` call in UIShell.mdx should document. Without a proper `component: Header` (or whichever primary entry point) and a `subcomponents: { HeaderNavigation, HeaderName, … }`, Storybook falls back to “undefined” as the primary tab and then picks up the named exports from the module for the sub-tabs – none of which have extracted props metadata. To fix this, UIShell.stories.js needs to be updated to include in its default export something like:

  component: Header,
  subcomponents: { HeaderNavigation, HeaderName, HeaderMenu, HeaderMenuItem, HeaderGlobalBar, … },
  parameters: { docs: { page: mdx } }

Once that metadata is present, the `<Props />` call in UIShell.mdx will correctly pull in and render the prop tables for each component.
1.bug_scenario: On the production Storybook page for the UIShell package (React v11.x), the “Component API” panel renders an “undefined” tab instead of the primary UIShell component, and then lists each subcomponent (Content, Header, HeaderMenuButton, HeaderName, HeaderNavigation, HeaderMenu, HeaderMenuItem, HeaderGlobalBar, etc.) – all of which show “No inputs found for this component.” In other words, Storybook’s Docs addon can’t find or associate the correct component definitions with the <Props /> call in the MDX docs, so no prop tables ever render.

2.explanation: The default export in UIShell.stories.js defines the story metadata (title, decorators, etc.) but omits the `component` and `subcomponents` fields that the Storybook Docs addon uses to generate its Props table. Without a `component` reference, the `<Props />` block in the UIShell MDX (or the auto-generated docs for each story) cannot resolve which component’s prop types to display—hence it shows “undefined.” Adding a `component: Header` (or the appropriate primary component) and listing all needed subcomponents under `subcomponents` in that default export will allow Storybook to locate and render the correct API tables.
2.bug_scenario: When viewing the UIShell stories (e.g. the “Fixed SideNav” story) in the published Storybook, the “Component API” props table appears with an “undefined” tab and shows “No inputs found for this component,” instead of rendering the prop tables for Header, HeaderMenuButton, SideNav, etc.
